en.headline: Uber plans Hong Kong ride-hailing licence application by end of October
en.dek: The platform’s local general manager said preparation is on track under the new regulatory regime, while Hong Kong users continue to drive strong demand for its Macau service.
body: Uber intends to submit its application for a Hong Kong ride-hailing platform licence by the end of October, its general manager for Hong Kong said on Tuesday, as the Transport Department’s licensing window remains open until 30 October.

Estyn Chung told reporters the company was working to meet the government’s requirements and was maintaining ongoing communication with the authorities. Under the new rules, applicants must demonstrate lawful operations in a city of at least 7.5 million people and average daily order volumes of more than 100,000 in at least two locations, among other financial and operational criteria.

Uber also noted that Hong Kong residents form the largest share of its Macau users after the service relaunched there earlier this year. The company said it continues to support local drivers with training and examination assistance during the transition period.

zh.headline: Uber料十月底前申請本港網約車牌照
zh.dek: 本地總經理表示正按新規管要求籌備，進度理想；同時指香港乘客仍是其澳門服務的最大用戶群。
body: Uber香港總經理周二表示，公司預計於十月底前向運輸署提交網約車服務平台牌照申請。運輸署現正接受申請，截止日期為十月三十日中午。
Estyn Chung指，公司正全力配合政府要求，並與當局保持溝通。新規定要求申請者須在人口750萬或以上的城市有合法營運經驗，並在至少兩個城市每日平均處理逾10萬宗訂單，另須符合資本及財務能力等條件。
Uber又指，自今年初在澳門重啟服務後，香港居民仍是其澳門用戶的最大比例。公司會繼續支援司機夥伴過渡，包括資助培訓及考試。
